climate.overview_html: The Climate Week NYC 2026 Opening Ceremony is underway today, September 21, at Lincoln Center (08:00–13:30 ET) — keynote addresses from Australia’s Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen and Antigua & Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne open the formal proceedings for the largest climate advocacy week of the year. The UNGA 81 General Debate begins Tuesday September 22 and Secretary-General Guterres convenes his high-level climate summit on Wednesday September 23, focused on accelerating the just energy transition and mobilising affordable climate finance for developing countries. The scientific backdrop grows more urgent with each day: Foster & Rahmstorf’s >98%-confidence confirmation that warming has accelerated faster than any prior decade in 177 years remains the capstone result; the Super El Niño is at or near seasonal peak (RONI +2.07°C, NDJ forecast +2.4–2.8°C); and Nepal’s UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a Himalayan catastrophe — remains active as heads of state arrive in New York, framing this as the highest-stakes Climate Week since Paris.

items.source: Climate Group / UNGA / UN Secretary-General / Columbia Climate School
items.headline: Climate Week NYC 2026 Opening Ceremony Underway Today September 21 (Lincoln Center, 08:00–13:30 ET); Theme: “Higher Stakes, Harder Choices / Real Momentum, Material Change”; UNGA 81 General Debate Begins September 22; Secretary-General Guterres High-Level Climate Summit September 23 — Just Transition Finance and Developing-Country Adaptation
items.summary: The Climate Week NYC 2026 Opening Ceremony is taking place today, September 21, at Lincoln Center (08:00–13:30 ET) under the theme 'Higher Stakes, Harder Choices / Real Momentum, Material Change.' Keynote speakers include Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen and Antigua & Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne. Climate Week NYC runs September 20–27 with more than 1,000 events across New York City. Tuesday September 22 marks the start of the UNGA 81 General Debate, where heads of state and government address the Assembly through September 28. On Wednesday September 23, Secretary-General António Guterres convenes a high-level meeting on climate action and the just transition focused on three pillars: (1) accelerating a just and orderly energy transition to renewables; (2) mobilising and scaling up affordable climate finance and investments for developing countries, given investment needs of USD 3.1–3.5 trillion per year by 2030; and (3) delivering adaptation and resilience support in an era of climate overshoot. More than 130 of 194 parties to the Paris Agreement submitted new NDCs by March 27, 2026, covering close to 75% of today's energy-related GHG emissions. The EU has set a 66–73% reduction by 2035 relative to 1990; Japan targets 73% by 2040 relative to 2013.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast Most Land Areas September–November; Super El Niño at Peak Season
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the confirmed Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026, with significant probability of record-breaking warmth in the tropics and sub-tropics. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.headline: Super El Niño Confirmed: Running ONI Crosses +2.0°C September 14 — First Super El Niño Since 2015–16; Peak Forecast NDJ 2026/27 at +2.4–2.8°C; WMO >95% Probability 2027 Sets Warmest Year Record
items.summary: The Running Oceanic Niño Index crossed the +2.0°C threshold on September 14, 2026, officially qualifying the current event as a Super El Niño — the first since 2015–16, which peaked at +2.6°C. The RONI reached +2.07°C. NOAA and WMO multi-model ensembles forecast a peak of +2.4–2.8°C for November–January 2026/27. Continued Atlantic hurricane suppression, drought in eastern Australia and SE Asia, and enhanced precipitation in the Horn of Africa are the primary near-term impacts. WMO assigns greater than 95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods ONGOING: ~1,446 Dead; ~6,669 Missing Including 587 Foreign Nationals; $820M+ Pledged; Nepal Climate Emergency Active; UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund Submission Initiated — First to Directly Implicate European Emissions in Himalayan Catastrophe
items.summary: Nepal's NDRRMA confirmed approximately 1,446 total deaths as of September 17, with approximately 6,669 persons missing including 587 foreign nationals from 34 countries. International pledges have reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament's national climate emergency declaration remains active. A formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission has been initiated — the first to directly implicate European-origin emissions in a documented Himalayan glacier catastrophe. ICIMOD's assessment found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume since 2020. The event remains the deadliest glacier-related disaster in recorded Himalayan history.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this window — framing it as the capstone scientific finding of Climate Week NYC 2026.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks and Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: Analysis quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology. France recorded its hottest summer ever with 2,025+ excess deaths. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Low Danube water forced Hungary's Paks nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures.

weather.overview_html: The headline September 21 story is Typhoon Dujuan’s landfall. Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan made landfall on the Boso Peninsula, Chiba Prefecture, at around midday September 21 JST with maximum sustained winds of 126 km/h and gusts to 180 km/h; 300+ mm of rain has already fallen over Kanto and Izu; Level 5 (highest) landslide emergency warnings are active for the Izu Peninsula and Level 4 evacuation orders cover Kanto coastal areas; JMA forecasts extratropical transition by September 22. Tokyo Game Show’s Monday session remains cancelled and the Asian Games Nagoya schedule was disrupted through the approach. In the Atlantic: Tropical Storm Fay remains active as of September 21 with possible brief intensification before post-tropical transition Tuesday September 22; no land threat; the 2026 Atlantic season remains at zero hurricanes through September 21 — the latest date in the satellite era without a hurricane. All other events (SE Asia haze, European wildfires, Nepal floods, Pakistan monsoon) show no material new update as of September 21 morning.

items.headline: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan MAKES LANDFALL September 21: Boso Peninsula, Chiba Prefecture, Midday JST; 126 km/h Sustained, Gusts 180 km/h; 300+ mm Rain Kanto/Izu; Level 5 Landslide Warning Izu; Level 4 Evacuation Kanto; Tokyo Game Show Monday Cancelled; Extratropical September 22
items.summary: Typhoon No. 25 Dujuan made landfall on the Boso Peninsula, Chiba Prefecture, at approximately midday JST on September 21, 2026. At landfall: maximum sustained winds 126 km/h, gusts to 180 km/h. Cumulative rainfall over Kanto and the Izu Peninsula exceeded 300 mm. JMA issued Level 5 (highest) landslide emergency warnings for the Izu Peninsula and Level 4 (evacuate now) orders for coastal Kanto. The system is forecast to curve NNE and become extratropical by September 22 as it moves off into the Pacific. Tokyo Game Show 2026's final day (Monday September 21) remains cancelled with online broadcast streams and refunds issued for 8,700 tickets. The 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya experienced schedule disruptions during the approach. Typhoon Dujuan is the strongest system to strike the Kanto region since 2019.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Fay UPDATED September 21: Still Active Open North Atlantic; Possible Brief Intensification; Post-Tropical Transition Tuesday September 22; No Land Threat; 2026 Atlantic Season Still Zero Hurricanes
items.summary: Tropical Storm Fay remains active in the open North Atlantic as of September 21, 2026 — the season's sixth named storm. NHC analysis indicates possible brief intensification before gradual weakening begins; post-tropical transition is expected Tuesday September 22 with no coastal watches, warnings, or land hazards in effect. The 2026 Atlantic season has still produced zero hurricanes through September 21, breaking the record for the latest date without a hurricane in the satellite era. Super El Niño-driven enhanced wind shear continues to suppress Atlantic tropical cyclone intensification. The previous record was September 18, 1966.

items.source: Time / ASMC ASEAN / Mongabay / ABC News Australia
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze ONGOING: 12 Million People Blanketed; 113,336 Respiratory Cases Indonesia (Sept 9); Japan CH-47 Chinooks Kalimantan Sept 12–19; Worst Indonesian Wildfires in 11 Years; Fires Through October/November
items.summary: No material update September 18–21. Status as of September 17: more than 12 million people blanketed in thick smog across Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. At least 200,000+ hectares burned across Borneo and Sumatra. Japan CH-47 Chinooks remained deployed in West Kalimantan through September 19. On September 14 Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Kuching ranked 1–3 globally for worst air quality. ASEAN Level 3 (highest) alert remains active. Indonesian authorities warn fires could continue through October or early November under Super El Niño-driven late rainy season suppression.

items.headline: Europe Wildfires ONGOING: 668,035 ha Burned Per EFFIS (As of September 16–17); Nearly Double 20-Year Average of 346,567 ha; Worst Season Since 2017; Extreme Fire Danger Continues Iberian Peninsula and Western Balkans
items.summary: No new EFFIS update as of September 21. Status as of September 16–17: 668,035 hectares burned in Europe in 2026, nearly double the 20-year average (2006–2025) of 346,567 hectares. Worst wildfire season since 2017. Extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans. The season is driven by western Europe's hottest summer on record (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) and drought accumulating from early spring.

items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert ONGOING: Monsoon Death Toll 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured; GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan Flash Flood Risk; Final Monsoon Active Phase Through Late September
items.summary: No new NDMA update found September 18–21. Status as of September 15: nationwide monsoon death toll 234 dead and 596 injured since late June. Flash flood risks cover Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan. Urban flooding continues in Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi. Final monsoon active phase extends through late September.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s flagship grid infrastructure contract remains 50Hertz awarding NSORe + Siemens Energy the LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC offshore converter platform on September 18 — NSORe’s second 2 GW 50Hertz contract in 2026, combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 value approximately €2.5 billion. The week also adds a landmark South Korean award: LS Marine Solution won a 156.9 billion won (~US$114 million) submarine cable installation contract for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm on September 18 — its largest-ever order at 2.2× its FY2025 revenue, and the first project in South Korea’s 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind belt. Africa adds its most significant new contract: EnerSynk + ZESCO’s 25-year, 500 MW Zambia Copperbelt PPA signed September 16 — the country’s largest-ever renewable contract, replacing drought-hit Zambezi hydropower for the copper-mining industry. In Europe: UK DCO consent for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan (September 15); Econergy’s €134.3 million entry into France via the Escofi 740 MW wind platform (September 15); and Masdar + Luxcara’s €5 billion+ Germany offshore wind + BESS MoU (September 14).

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform Contract to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion to NSORe; Topside Rostock-Warnemünde, Jacket Vlissingen
items.summary: German transmission system operator 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) joint venture and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following the LanWin6 award in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles system design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. The topside is fabricated at Neptun Werft in Rostock-Warnemünde, Germany; the steel jacket at Smulders in Vlissingen, the Netherlands. Combined contract value attributable to NSORe for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion. LanWin3 is part of Germany's programme to connect the offshore wind build-out in the North Sea to the onshore grid at scale, with Germany's 2026 offshore tenders requiring co-located battery storage.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Offshore Wind Project; Largest-Ever LS Marine Order (2.2× FY2025 Revenue); First Project in 8.2 GW Sinan Offshore Wind Belt; Cable Installation 2026–2028
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (approximately US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2 times its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund specifically for offshore wind, and marks the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt off South Jeolla Province. Cable installation is scheduled 2026–2028. The contract reflects South Korea's acceleration of large-scale offshore wind procurement following the government's target of 14.3 GW by 2030.

items.headline: Zambia Inks 25-Year PPA for 500 MW Solar Project — EnerSynk + ZESCO Copperbelt; Zambia’s Largest-Ever Renewable Contract; Replaces Drought-Hit Zambezi Hydropower for Copper Industry
items.summary: EnerSynk and ZESCO Ltd signed a 25-year PPA on September 16 for a 500 MW solar PV project in Zambia's Copperbelt — the country's largest-ever renewable energy contract. The project specifically targets the copper-mining industry's power supply chain, which accounts for approximately 70% of Zambia's total power demand. The plant reduces ZESCO's dependence on hydropower repeatedly curtailed in 2026 by drought driven by the positive IOD and Super El Niño.

items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Complete; Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households
items.summary: UK Secretary of State approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire, completing the full regulatory package for Morecambe. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15 — Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio: 128 MW operational, 34 MW under construction (target 2027), 147 MW advanced development, and 432 MW early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year French CfDs at above €80/MWh.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News / Energy Global
items.headline: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — Signed During UAE State Visit to Berlin; Potential Expansion to Other European Markets
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara signed an MoU on September 14 to explore joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. Germany's 2026 offshore wind tenders require co-located BESS, driving this market. The partnership targets co-development, financing, and ownership, with possible expansion to other European markets.

science.overview_html: The window’s headline new result is Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. Nature Climate Change (September 16): heat-related labor productivity loss quantified at US$41 per tonne CO2 (90% CI $1–108) in 2025 — the second-largest component of the social cost of carbon after heat mortality, with losses concentrated in South, East, and Southeast Asia and Africa; agricultural damage revised down from $95 to $29/tonne CO2 using AR6. The foundational warming-rate result carries forward: Foster & Rahmstorf GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17 (September 16): >98%-confidence acceleration since ~2015, faster than any prior decade in the 177-year record across five datasets. Stratospheric chemistry: van Herpen et al. Nature Communications (September 15) on Hunga Tonga’s Cl-radical CH4 oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day, absent from CMIP7 models. AI weather forecasting: ECMWF arXiv:2609.03210 fine-tunes AIFS-CRPS on IMERG satellite precipitation, achieving +19% medium-range CRPSS and +57% BSS for extreme rainfall globally; and TailWeather (arXiv:2609.12496) provides the first global 0.25° extremes benchmark from ERA5 1981–2022 targeting tail skill rather than average accuracy.

items.source: Nature Climate Change / UC Davis / phys.org
items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Heat-Related Labor Productivity Loss = US$41/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> (90% CI $1–108) in 2025 — Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al.; Second-Largest SC-CO<sub>2</sub> Component After Heat Mortality; Agricultural Damage Revised Down to $29/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> Using AR6; Losses Concentrated South/East/SE Asia and Africa
items.meta: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02749-z · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. quantify heat-related labor productivity loss as a standalone component of the social cost of carbon, finding a central estimate of US$41 per tonne CO₂ (90% CI $1–108) when evaluated in 2025 dollars against a 2°C pathway. This makes labor productivity the second-largest SC-CO₂ component after heat mortality in the updated accounting — a significant upward revision from prior estimates. Agricultural damage was simultaneously revised down from US$95 to US$29 per tonne CO₂ using IPCC AR6 methods and updated dose-response functions. Losses are geographically concentrated in South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa — regions with both high outdoor labor shares and high climate vulnerability. The result has immediate implications for climate damage assessments used in litigation and regulatory cost-benefit analysis.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Faster Than Any Prior Decade in 177-Year Record After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.meta: Foster & Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Vol. 53, Issue 17 · doi:10.1029/2025GL118804 · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for climate damage claims, including the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active in this window — framing it as the capstone scientific finding of Climate Week NYC 2026.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed Anomalous CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From CMIP7 Models; Potential Net Cooling Offset in Large-Eruption/SAI Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane-oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS limb-emission satellite observations, the authors quantify CH₄ oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km altitude, sufficient to explain the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210 — ECMWF: Fine-Tuning AIFS-CRPS on IMERG Satellite Precipitation Achieves +19% Medium-Range CRPSS for Precipitation and +57% BSS for Extreme Rainfall Globally; Better at Tropical Storms and Drizzle; Physics Model Still Better for Heaviest Events
items.summary: ECMWF researchers fine-tuned the AIFS-CRPS probabilistic AI weather model on NASA IMERG satellite-derived precipitation observations to improve medium-range precipitation skill. The fine-tuned model achieves a +19% improvement in Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score (CRPSS) for medium-range precipitation forecasts and a +57% improvement in Brier Skill Score (BSS) for extreme rainfall events globally compared to the base AIFS-CRPS. Performance improvements are strongest for tropical systems and light-to-moderate precipitation (drizzle and stratiform rain); the traditional physics-based IFS model retains skill advantages at the heaviest precipitation thresholds. The result demonstrates that operational AI weather models can be significantly improved for precipitation without full retraining by domain-specific fine-tuning on dedicated observational datasets.

items.headline: TailWeather (arXiv 2609.12496) — Liu, Boy & Makkonen: Global 0.25° Land-Only Extremes Benchmark From ERA5 1981–2022; Labels Heatwaves, Cold Waves, Heavy Precipitation, Extreme Wind, Drought; Ordinal Severity Tiers + Numerical Intensity Scores vs 1991–2020 Climatology; Addresses AI Weather Model Evaluation Gap at the Tail
items.meta: Liu, Boy & Makkonen · arXiv:2609.12496 · September 2026 · cs.LG / physics.ao-ph
items.summary: TailWeather introduces a global 0.25° land-only benchmark dataset constructed from ERA5 reanalysis (1981–2022) specifically designed to evaluate AI weather model skill on extreme events rather than average conditions. The dataset labels five hazard types — heatwaves, cold waves, heavy precipitation, extreme wind, and drought — with both ordinal severity tiers (mild/moderate/severe/extreme) and continuous numerical intensity scores benchmarked against the 1991–2020 climatology. The authors identify a systematic evaluation gap: standard benchmark datasets (WeatherBench, ClimateBench) measure skill on average or near-normal conditions, while skill on tail events — where societal impact is highest — is neither measured nor optimised. TailWeather allows model rankings to differ substantially from those produced by standard benchmarks, particularly for rare and compound extremes.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion — Fifth Consecutive Year of >$100 Billion Global Insured Nat-Cat Losses
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20, 2026 highlights three developments in the catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities market: MembersCap has launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel industry loss warranty (ILW) structure designed to expand ILS investor access; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a new, previously unbondable peril (specific peril undisclosed at launch), representing a structural expansion of the cat bond market’s risk frontier; and CalPERS’ insurance-linked securities holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026, cementing its position as the largest institutional investor in the cat bond asset class. The bulletin contextualises these developments against the fifth consecutive year of global insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding US$100 billion, which has sustained the structural case for ILS as a portfolio diversifier uncorrelated with equity and credit risk premia.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Newberry Volcano, Oregon; Project Athena Drilling 750°F (400°C) Target
items.body_html: Mazama Energy, the Newberry Volcano (Oregon) superhot engineered geothermal system developer, raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest engineered geothermal system ever built: a 629°F (331°C) EGS at Newberry in 2025, proving reservoir creation, connectivity, and heat recovery. Its second well, Project Athena, reached 10,350 feet in 15 days — 80% faster than the 2025 well — and is drilling a further mile toward a 750°F (400°C) target; at that temperature a single well delivers up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F (200°C) well while using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells. The raise reflects growing major-oil-company conviction that superhot geothermal, with its baseload output profile and minimal surface footprint, can anchor firm-power supply in a grid increasingly dominated by variable renewables.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions to Be Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing that only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently covered by insurance — a structural gap that leaves households, farmers, and municipalities absorbing the remainder and creates sovereign fiscal risk during compound extreme-weather years. The Alliance will bring together insurers, investors, risk modellers, regulators, and policyholders to develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric insurance instruments — paying on measurable thresholds such as rainfall levels or temperatures rather than assessed losses — for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 668,035 ha per EFFIS September 17 with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics said the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product is a grid monitoring device that harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating the need for external power supplies, batteries, or fibre-optic ground wires. The device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data to grid operators; the self-powered design makes it viable for remote high-voltage corridors where conventional monitoring costs are prohibitive, directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and the NATO dual-use energy security priority driving NIF’s participation.
